name: US Constitution and Constitutional Law
description: Constitutional structure, amendments and landmark Supreme Court cases.

content.answer: The legislative branch (Congress).

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: The executive branch (President).

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: The judicial branch (Supreme Court and inferior courts).

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: The Constitution, federal statutes and treaties are the supreme law of the land.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Protects religion, speech, press, assembly and petition.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Right to keep and bear arms.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Protects against unreasonable searches and seizures; warrants require probable cause.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Grand jury, double jeopardy, self-incrimination, due process, takings clause.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Speedy public trial, impartial jury, counsel, confrontation of witnesses.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Bans excessive bail and fines and cruel and unusual punishment.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Powers not delegated to the federal government are reserved to the states or the people.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Citizenship, due process and equal protection applied to the states.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Gives Congress power to regulate commerce among the states (Art. I, section 8).

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Established judicial review.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Upheld implied powers (Necessary and Proper Clause) and federal supremacy over state taxation.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Broad reading of congressional commerce power.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Segregated public schools violate Equal Protection.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Suspects in custody must be warned of rights before interrogation.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Right to appointed counsel for indigent felony defendants.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Exclusionary rule applies to the states.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Public-official defamation requires actual malice.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Students do not shed free speech rights at school absent substantial disruption.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Roe (1973) recognized a constitutional abortion right; Dobbs v. Jackson (2022) overruled it.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: The Fourteenth Amendment protects same-sex marriage.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Law must serve a compelling interest and be narrowly tailored; applies to fundamental rights and suspect classifications.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Law must be rationally related to a legitimate government interest; the default standard.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Injury in fact, causation, and redressability.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Natural-born citizen, age 35, and 14 years a resident (Art. II).

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Proposed by two-thirds of both houses (or a convention); ratified by three-fourths of states.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: Senators serve 6 years; Representatives serve 2 years.

cards.sourceRef: U.S. Constitution (archives.gov); Chemerinsky, Constitutional Law (Wolters Kluwer)

content.answer: The House impeaches by majority vote; the Senate tries with a two-thirds vote to convict.
